_readme: Provenance manifest for every hardcoded real-world fact in this repo's calculators. Each entry names the real external source, its real update cadence, when it was last verified against that source (by whom/what commit), whether an automated check exists, and that check's actual verified status. Update this file in the same commit as any data fix. Do not add an entry with a fabricated or unverified source - if a fact's real source hasn't been checked, mark automated_check.status as "missing" and last_verified.method as "never independently verified", don't invent a plausible-looking entry.

entries.description: Federal income tax brackets, standard deduction, and FICA figures used by the take-home pay calculator.

real_source.name: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (federal brackets/deduction) + SSA wage base announcement (Oct 24, 2025)
real_source.real_cadence: annual - IRS typically publishes the following tax year's figures in October/November; SSA wage base announced around the same time

last_verified.method: manual audit - downloaded the real Rev. Proc. PDF, cross-verified every bracket threshold against the document's own stated cumulative-tax dollar amounts before trusting it

automated_check.behavior: Scrapes the IRS newsroom page for the target tax year, falls back to CPI-based estimation if the page is unpublished or unparseable, sends a Slack alert if both fail. Auto-commits only on a genuine parsed/estimated change.
automated_check.known_gaps: Compares the file's own year header to the current calendar year, so it won't attempt to fetch next year's real IRS data until the calendar rolls over in January - misses the real Oct-Dec publication window by roughly 2-3 months. Worth changing to check in October regardless of calendar year. Also does not cover STATE_TAX_RATES in the same file (see next entry) - the workflow's git-diff check watches the whole file, but the update script itself only ever touches the federal bracket/deduction section.
automated_check.backstop: Also covered by the generic .github/workflows/data-freshness-check.yml (added 2026-09-08), which Slack-alerts if next_check_due passes without this entry being re-verified - a second-layer reminder in case the live scrape above ever fails silently.

entries.description: Simplified single effective marginal rate per state (at $100,000 single-filer taxable income, reverse-engineered as the reference income that matched this file's pre-existing methodology), used as a proxy since this calculator doesn't model full state bracket schedules.

real_source.name: Tax Foundation, "2026 State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets"
real_source.real_cadence: annual, typically published early in the calendar year for that year

last_verified.method: manual audit - downloaded Tax Foundation's real XLSX bracket dataset, parsed full bracket schedules for all 51 jurisdictions, computed the real marginal rate at $100K for each

automated_check.note: The existing update-data.yml workflow watches lib/tax-data.ts for diffs but its script never touches this section - a real state-level rate change would go completely undetected there. As of 2026-09-08, the generic data-freshness-check.yml job Slack-alerts once next_check_due passes, but it does not fetch or verify Tax Foundation's real data itself - someone still has to re-run the manual audit. A real live check (like the federal-tax-data entry has) has not been built for this table.
